clauses.current_legal_basis: The held original (29 FR 227) states no end for this paragraph. The held Executive Order 13286 section 68 (68 FR 10619, 10629, effective March 1, 2003) amended it by substituting the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Secretary of the Treasury, which treats the order as continuing. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, read for coverage (U.S. Code release point 119-121 current through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register catalog dispositions) show no revocation, supersession or other ending. Checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: The paragraph authorizes the Secretary of Defense, for the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps, and (as originally written) the Secretary of the Treasury, for the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, to prescribe regulations under which the United Nations Medal and Service Ribbon may be accepted by eligible members of the armed forces, and requires the Secretary of State's concurrence in determinations about service areas and purposes. Executive Order 13286 section 68, effective March 1, 2003 (section 92), struck the words the Secretary of the Treasury and inserted the Secretary of Homeland Security (before: the Secretary of the Treasury; after: the Secretary of Homeland Security). The clause continues as amended; the held text of the paragraph has no end date or condition, and no later order revoking or superseding it was found. It is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11139 of January 7, 1964 (29 FR 227; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11139.txt, read in full) is a single paragraph. It authorizes the Secretary of Defense (for members of the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps) and the Secretary of the Treasury (for members of the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy) to prescribe regulations under which the United Nations Medal and Service Ribbon may be accepted by eligible members of the armed forces, and requires that a determination that service in a particular area or for a particular purpose is a justifiable basis for acceptance be made with the concurrence of the Secretary of State. The text states no date, duration, condition or expiry. The only later instrument found is Executive Order 13286 section 68 (68 FR 10619, 10629; effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92), which struck the Secretary of the Treasury and inserted the Secretary of Homeland Security; it is recorded as a later event on the clause. A search of the held Federal Register texts of orders numbered above 11139 for citations of this order found only Executive Order 13286. The Office of the Federal Register disposition note for the order reads that it was amended by Executive Order 13286, February 28, 2003, and names no revocation or supersession. The bounded searches current-law:usc (one hit, the printed Executive Order 13286 note listing section 68 as an amendment of this order), current-law:ecfr (no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (one hit, the Executive Order 13286 amendment) show no revocation. The clause is therefore operative on 2026-10-14. No current Code or CFR text printing this order is held, so the current predicate rests on the held original, the held amendment and the three bounded searches (the original_plus_bounded_search route). Standing note on sources: the original is held as a machine text layer of the official Federal Register page; check the page before relying on quotations.

savings.reason: The order grants authority to prescribe regulations and fixes a concurrence requirement; it creates no one-time act that has been performed and used up, and no grant of money or property. No savings or residual effect needs separate treatment: the regulation-making authority and the concurrence rule are the continuing command itself, recorded as operative. No transferred or accrued rights are claimed.
